source.name: VocabBuilder starter set (Polish)
source.notes: Hand-written by an AI assistant (Claude) as a small starter set for VocabBuilder. Not corpus-derived: curatedOrder is a teaching order, not a frequency rank. Review and edit freely.

senses.note: Literally 'good day'; used from morning until evening.

examples.text: Dzień dobry, czy jest wolny stolik?
examples.translation: Hello, is there a free table?

examples.text: Dzień dobry, nazywam się Anna Nowak.
examples.translation: Hello, my name is Anna Nowak.

grammar.notes: The standard polite greeting. In the evening: dobry wieczór. Informal: cześć.

examples.translation: Hi! What's new with you?
Bye, see you tomorrow!

grammar.notes: Informal: for friends, family and anyone you call ty. Used for both hello and goodbye.

examples.translation: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you, everything is delicious.

grammar.notes: Literally 'I thank'. For something: dziękuję za + accusative (dziękuję za pomoc). Informal: dzięki.

senses.note: The reply to dziękuję; also said when handing something over.

examples.translation: Please speak a little more slowly.
Here you are, this is for you.

grammar.notes: Literally 'I ask'. proszę + infinitive is a polite request. To order or ask for something: poproszę… 'I'd like…'.

examples.translation: Yes, I speak a little Polish.
Yes, of course, I'll be glad to help.

senses.note: Before verbs: nie wiem 'I don't know'.

examples.translation: No, thanks, I don't want any.
That's not my phone.

grammar.notes: A negated verb takes the genitive instead of the accusative: mam czas → nie mam czasu.

examples.translation: Sorry, I didn't know about that.
I'm very sorry for being late.

grammar.notes: Literally 'I apologize'. For something: przepraszam za + accusative (przepraszam za spóźnienie).

examples.translation: What do you want for dinner?
What are you thinking about now?

grammar.notes: Declined: czego, czemu, czym (o czym 'about what').

examples.translation: Excuse me, where's the restroom?
Where's the nearest pharmacy?

grammar.notes: Location. For direction ('where to') the standard word is dokąd (colloquially also gdzie).

examples.translation: What's your name?
How do you say this in Polish?

examples.text: Mama i tata są w domu.
examples.translation: Mom and Dad are at home.

examples.text: Chleb i masło są na stole.
examples.translation: The bread and butter are on the table.

grammar.notes: A more formal synonym is oraz.

examples.text: Chciałbym pójść, ale nie mam czasu.
examples.translation: I'd like to go, but I don't have time.

examples.text: Tu jest drogo, ale bardzo smacznie.
examples.translation: It's expensive here, but very tasty.
Are you home yet?
The weather will be nice tomorrow.

grammar.notes: Irregular: jestem, jesteś, jest, jesteśmy, jesteście, są. Stress is normally on the next-to-last syllable, but in past forms like byliśmy, byliście the standard stress falls one syllable earlier (BY-liś-my).

examples.translation: I want to buy a new phone.
What do you want to do at the weekend?

grammar.notes: More polite: chciałbym (man) / chciałabym (woman) 'I would like'.

senses.note: Perfective partner in the sense 'to say, to tell': powiedzieć.

examples.translation: Do you speak English?
My mom speaks very fast.

grammar.notes: mówić po polsku = to speak Polish.

examples.translation: I don't understand, could you repeat that?
Do you understand what he's saying?

grammar.notes: Perfective: zrozumieć (zrozumiem, zrozumiał).

senses.note: To know a fact or a piece of information.

examples.translation: I don't know where he lives.
Do you know what time it is?

grammar.notes: wiedzieć = to know a fact (wiem, że…); znać = to know a person, place or thing. Irregular: wiem, wiesz, wie, wiemy, wiecie, wiedzą.

examples.translation: Could you help me, sir?
I can't today, sorry.

grammar.notes: g/ż alternation: mogę, możesz, może, możemy, możecie, mogą. On its own, może also means 'maybe'.

examples.translation: He's a very good person.

examples.text: Dzisiaj jest tu za dużo ludzi.
examples.translation: There are too many people here today.

grammar.notes: The plural is a different word: ludzie, ludzi.

examples.text: Czy mogę prosić o szklankę wody?
examples.translation: Could I have a glass of water, please?
I always take water with me on a walk.

grammar.notes: d → dzi in the locative: w wodzie.

examples.translation: That's a good idea.
Do you know a good restaurant?

grammar.notes: Plural: dobrzy for groups including men, dobre for everything else. Comparative: lepszy 'better'. Adverb: dobrze 'well, OK'.

examples.translation: I'm at work right now.
I can't talk right now.
What day is it today?
Today I'm working from home.

grammar.notes: Shorter synonym: dziś.

examples.translation: Excuse me, is this seat free?
I've been living here for a year.

grammar.notes: Shorter synonym: tu. Used for both location and direction (Chodź tutaj! 'Come here!').

examples.translation: I really like Warsaw.

examples.text: Bardzo mi miło, mam na imię Ola.
examples.translation: Nice to meet you, my name is Ola.

examples.text: Mieszkam w Warszawie od dwóch lat.
examples.translation: I've been living in Warsaw for two years.
Where does your family live?

grammar.notes: mieszkać = to live somewhere; żyć = to be alive, to live (a life).

examples.translation: What are you doing tonight?
We always do this together.

grammar.notes: Imperative: rób! Perfective: zrobić.

examples.translation: What did he tell you yesterday?
I'll tell you tomorrow, OK?

grammar.notes: Perfective, so its present-tense forms refer to the future: powiem = 'I'll say'. Conjugated like wiedzieć: powiem, powiesz, powie, powiemy, powiecie, powiedzą.

senses.note: To know a person, place or thing.

examples.translation: Do you know his phone number?
I know this restaurant, it's great.

grammar.notes: znać takes a direct object (znam go, znam to miasto); for facts use wiedzieć.

examples.translation: Our house is very old.
I get home at six.

grammar.notes: w domu = at home; do domu = (to) home.

examples.translation: I'm still at work.
He's looking for a new job.

grammar.notes: w pracy = at work; do pracy = to work. szukać takes the genitive: szukam pracy.

examples.translation: This is my old friend.

examples.text: W sobotę spotykam się z przyjaciółmi.
examples.translation: On Saturday I'm meeting up with friends.

grammar.notes: A close friend; a female friend is przyjaciółka. For a buddy or colleague, kolega / koleżanka is common. Irregular plural: przyjaciele, przyjaciół.

examples.translation: I have a very big family.
I really miss my family.

grammar.notes: tęsknić za + instrumental = to miss.

examples.translation: I often call my mom.
Mom, I'm home!

grammar.notes: Vocative when addressing her: mamo! dzwonić do + genitive = to call someone.

examples.translation: I don't have time today.
We still have a bit of time.

grammar.notes: To ask the time: Która (jest) godzina? czasem also means 'sometimes'.

examples.translation: I work five days a week.
It was a very long day.

grammar.notes: Irregular stem: dzień → dnia, dni. Nominative plural also dnie.

examples.translation: See you tomorrow at nine!
Tomorrow is my day off.

senses.note: One direction, on foot, at a particular time.

examples.translation: I'm going home now.
Where are you going so early?

grammar.notes: Irregular past: szedł, szła, szli. For habitual or round trips use chodzić; by vehicle use jechać.

senses.note: One direction, by car, bus, train etc.

examples.translation: Tomorrow we're going to Kraków.
I'm taking the bus to work.

grammar.notes: For habitual or round trips use jeździć. Transport in the instrumental: autobusem, pociągiem.

examples.translation: I don't eat meat.
What do you eat for breakfast?

grammar.notes: Irregular: jem, jesz, je, jemy, jecie, jedzą; past jadł, jadła.

examples.translation: She drinks coffee with milk.
I don't drink coffee in the evening.

grammar.notes: Present stem pij-: piję, pijesz… piją.

examples.translation: I'll buy bread and milk.
Where did you buy this jacket?

grammar.notes: Perfective; imperfective kupować (kupuję).

examples.translation: I'll do it tomorrow morning.
Who took this photo?

grammar.notes: Perfective of robić: zrobię = 'I will do (and finish)'.

examples.translation: Please buy some bread and cheese.
We're out of bread.
Would you like some tea with lemon?
We drink tea in the kitchen.

grammar.notes: t → ci in the locative: w herbacie.

examples.translation: Let's go for a coffee after work.
Your coffee has gone cold.
I'm going to the shop for bread.

examples.text: W tym sklepie wszystko jest tańsze.
examples.translation: Everything is cheaper in this shop.

grammar.notes: do sklepu 'to the shop', w sklepie 'in the shop'. po + accusative = to go and get: po chleb.

examples.translation: I don't have any money on me.
This money is for shopping.

grammar.notes: Used in the plural: te pieniądze 'this money'. ą → ę in other forms: pieniędzy.

senses.note: być złym na kogoś = to be angry with someone.

examples.translation: In my opinion that's a bad idea.
Are you angry with me?

grammar.notes: Plural: źli for groups including men, złe for everything else. Comparative: gorszy 'worse'. Adverb: źle 'badly'.

examples.translation: Kraków is a big city.
They live in a big house.

grammar.notes: Comparative: większy 'bigger'. wielki = great, huge.

examples.translation: We have a small apartment in the center.
My son is still little.

grammar.notes: Comparative: mniejszy 'smaller'.

examples.translation: This is my new phone.
I wish you a Happy New Year!

senses.note: In greetings and letters: Drodzy przyjaciele!

examples.translation: This restaurant is too expensive.
Dear friends, all the best!

grammar.notes: Plural: drodzy for groups including men, drogie for everything else. Comparative: droższy. Don't confuse with the noun droga 'road'.

examples.translation: This soup is very tasty.
Mom makes really tasty pierogi.

grammar.notes: Plural for things: smaczne (smaczne pierogi). Adverb: smacznie.

examples.translation: We live in the city center.

examples.text: W moim mieście jest piękny park.
examples.translation: There's a beautiful park in my town.

grammar.notes: Note the stem change in the locative: w mieście.

examples.translation: What street do you live on?
This street is very busy.

grammar.notes: na ulicy / przy ulicy = on a street (in addresses).

examples.translation: I'll call you in a week.

examples.text: W tym tygodniu jestem bardzo zajęty.
examples.translation: I'm very busy this week.

grammar.notes: Irregular stem: tydzień → tygodnia, w tygodniu. za tydzień = in a week.

examples.translation: He's on the phone right now.
I can't find my phone.

grammar.notes: rozmawiać przez telefon = to talk on the phone. A mobile phone is often called komórka.

examples.translation: I'm learning Polish.
How many foreign languages do you know?
The doctor asked me to show my tongue.

grammar.notes: uczyć się takes the genitive: uczę się języka polskiego.

examples.translation: They have two children.
Our child is already asleep.

grammar.notes: Irregular plural: dzieci, dzieci, dzieciom, dziećmi. dwoje dzieci = two children.

examples.translation: Wash your hands before eating.
I broke my arm as a child.

grammar.notes: Irregular plural: ręce, rąk, rękom, rękami (or rękoma).

examples.translation: I've had a headache since this morning.
I still need to wash my hair.

grammar.notes: Boli mnie głowa = I have a headache (literally 'my head hurts me'). umyć głowę = to wash one's hair.

examples.translation: I need to see a doctor.
We need to call a doctor quickly.

grammar.notes: Animate: accusative = genitive (wezwać lekarza).

examples.translation: I've already bought a train ticket.
Two tickets to Gdańsk, please.

grammar.notes: After 2–4 the nominative plural is used: dwa bilety; from 5 the genitive plural: pięć biletów.
